0:
Remnants of the former
Principality of Zeon's
forces. They still wage
guerrilla war on the UCE
across the Earth Sphere.
1:
A remnant group of the
former Principality of
Zeon's forces, led by
Aiguille Delaz. Heir to
former Zeon thought, it
seeks to establish
Spacenoid self-rule.
After stealing Gundam
Unit 2 from the UCE, it
declared war on the UCE.
2:
A lunar empire founded
by some lunar
emigrants.
Under Marshal Guiltorre,
it declared independence
to defy Earth's tyranny.
It has fought the UCE
ever since, and lately it
has stepped up its
invasion of Earth.
3:
A research group formed
inside Orphan, and the
Orphan believers
gathered there.

They work to raise
Orphan, bound for the
galaxy, out of the
atmosphere.
The Reclaimers also have
a combat unit that pilots
Organic Machines called
Grand Chers and, as
Orphan's Antibodies,
eliminates the forces
hostile to it.
4:
Unidentified unmanned
weapons that have often
raided Earth in recent
years. The name comes
from the countless
bug-like mechs and
warships sent out of
gates called Chulips.
5:
Descendants of lunar
emigrants whom Earth
exiled to Mars.
Later driven from Mars
too by a nuclear attack,
they survived by the
power of ancient ruins
found near Jupiter.
After long preparation,
they take up arms, with
Gekiganger 3 as
scripture, for revenge on
the Earth that took their
home.
"Jovian Federation" is
short for "Jovian Sphere
Ganymede, Callisto,
Europa and Other Moon
and Asteroid States
Anti-Earth Joint Union."
6:
A private army led by
Drake Luft, exiled from
the other world of
Byston Well to the
surface. Bent on
dominating the surface,
Drake has eyed the
Organic Machines, which
run on a bio-energy akin
to Aura Power, and plots
to subdue Earth by
means of Orphan.
So, while in a temporary
alliance with the
Reclaimers, who stand
alone against the other
powers, he waits for a
chance to seize Orphan.
7:
The governing power
that rules the Pentagona
World, a binary star
system in outer space.

Its ruler is Oldna
Poseidal.
Eyeing something in the
Earth Sphere, it sends an
expedition led by Giwaza
Lowau to obtain it.
8:
A military state centered
on the planet Grados in
the Burdoria system.
Claiming to guide
primitive alien cultures,
it has conquered many
worlds. Under Le Cain,
son of Gresco, admiral of
the Earth invasion fleet,
it invades Earth.
9:
A race of giants with
nothing called culture,
made solely for battle.

Made up only of men,
they have long warred
with the Meltrandi.
The Zentradi forces
operate in over 1000
main fleets. Of these, the
Boddole Flagship Fleet,
deployed in Earth's
direction, is pursuing
the Macross for some
reason.
10:
A warrior race of giants
made up only of women.

They have been at war
with the Zentradi for
many years.
To seize the Protoculture
legacy left in Orphan, on
Earth, they launch an
invasion of Earth.
11:
A former UCE developer.
With his exceptional
talent, he led a
new-weapon project to
defend the Earth Sphere,
but vanished when it fell
through. He was later
found to be commanding
obsolete units as a
private army, and
declared war on the UCE.
What he did while
missing, and where he
hid, is completely
unknown.
12:
An unidentified machine
appearing in various
places.
It acts strangely: it joins
battles as a third party,
sides with one force,
then withdraws.
Besides high combat
ability, it has been
confirmed to control
bombardment from
satellite orbit.
Its pilot and affiliation
are entirely unknown.
13:
The berserk form of the
"Ultimate Gundam," built
to renew Earth on three
theories: self-evolution,
self-repair,
self-replication. Stolen
by Kyoji Kasshu, it ran
amok in an accident as
he fled.
The UCE is tracking it.
14:
The Earth Sphere's
governing body, formed
to rule and secure it as a
whole. Made of
Earth-based groups like
the Earth Federation,
UESF and U.N., it has no
army of its own, only
troops pooled from them.
So the strongest military
members gain the most
say, making the Earth
Federation its de facto
leader. Lately it has
founded the UCE Design
Bureau and more to
build its own forces, free
of its members.
15:
The Earth Sphere's
governing body, formed
to rule and secure it as a
whole. Made of
Earth-based groups like
the Earth Federation,
UESF and U.N., it has no
army of its own, only
troops pooled from them.
So the strongest military
members gain the most
say, making the Earth
Federation its de facto
leader.
Lately it has founded
the UCE Design Bureau
and more to build its
own forces, free of its
members.
Later, the Delaz Fleet's
call-to-arms speech
showed the world the
Gundam GP02,
nuclear-armed in breach
of the Antarctic Treaty.
So the Earth Federation
faction lost influence in
the UCE, and UCE
sovereignty passed to
the United Earth Space
Force.
16:
One of the UCE's main
member organizations,
and the largest within it.
On the strength of its
record in the last great
war, it rose with its
military to become a
major power in the UCE.
It still holds the reins of
UCE administration.
17:
The main armed force of
the United Earth, and
one of the UCE's main
member organizations.
The United Earth also
has ground, naval and
air forces, but Space
Force units can fully
operate under gravity, so
the Space Force is by far
the largest.
18:
A UCE assault landing
ship.
It serves as mothership
to the prototypes of the
Gundam Development
Project. Its captain is
Eyphar Sinapus, of the
Earth Federation.
19:
An intelligence agency
within the UCE.

It investigates and
counters the moves of
hostile organizations.
It is commanded by
Lady Une.
"Preventer" means
"firefighter."
20:
The UCE's own
new-weapon development
division. Founded when
Gun Ark development
began. Staffed with chief
researcher Barkholz and
other gifted developers
proven in the One Year
War and more, it holds
strong sway in the UCE.
21:
A warship organized to
oppose the Reclaimers,
who seek to raise
Orphan.
It carries a new type of
engine called the
Organic Engine, and a
Brain Powerd team is
deployed aboard.
Its captain is Irene
Carrier.
22:
A cutting-edge ship built
independently by Nergal
Heavy Industries. Using
Martian lost technology,
from the central
computer Omoikane to
the Distortion Field
(dimension-warping
barrier) and Gravity
Blast (gravity wave
cannon), it has great
fighting power.
Its captain is Yurika
Misumaru.
23:
A new battleship built
by the UCE.

It was made by refitting
an alien warship that
fell to Earth in the past.
It has mechanisms
beyond current Earth
technology, such as a
space-jump drive called
fold and a variable
structure that transforms
into Attack Mode.
Its captain is Bruno J.
Global.
24:
A battleship exiled from
the other world of
Byston Well to the
surface. It runs on Aura
Power, so it is called an
Aura Ship. As an enemy
of the Drake Army, it
comes to aid UCE
operations on the
surface. It is commanded
by Ciela Lapana, Queen
of the Kingdom of Na.
25:
A resistance group
fighting Poseidal's rule
over the Pentagona
World. It is led by Daba
Myroad.
Pursuing the Giwaza
Fleet sent by Poseidal,
some of its members,
Daba among them, have
come as far as the Earth
Sphere.
26:
The largest private
company in the Earth
Sphere. A general maker
of everything from home
appliances to arms, it is
known above all for its
mobile suits.
It co-developed the
Gundam prototypes of
the UCE's Gundam
Development Project.
27:
An Asian corporate
group. Deeply involved
in developing Mars from
early on, it has great
clout for a private firm.
It is also known for
building the battleship
Nadesico with ancient
Martian technology.
28:
Leader of the Delaz
Fleet. Carrying on the
former Principality of
Zeon's ideal of
"Spacenoid self-rule," he
declared war on the UCE.
29:
Commander of the Cima
Fleet. As part of the
Delaz Fleet, she fights
the UCE under Aiguille
Delaz's command.
30:
An engineer at Anaheim
Electronics.

In charge of developing
Gundam Units 1 and 2,
she joined the Albion for
their evaluation tests.
She also stays with the
ship in the pursuit after
the Gundam's theft.
Her attachment to the
Gundams is second to
none.
31:
An Earth Federation
space force Commodore.
As Gundam Development
Project head, he leads
the bid to retake the
stolen Gundam Unit 2.
32:
Admiral of the United
Earth Space Force.
Named its supreme
commander when it took
charge of the UCE. With
the Albion as his own
special task force, he
directs efforts to quell
conflicts everywhere.
He is also the real father
of Nadesico captain
Yurika Misumaru.
33:
Marshal of the Unified
Empire of Giganos. A
staunch elitist, he waged
strategic war on the UCE
and its antiquated order.
34:
A Giganos lieutenant
colonel.
He assassinated Marshal
Guiltorre, who held back
from indiscriminate mass
driver attacks on Earth.
Framing Meio Plato for
it, he became Supreme
Leader of the Unified
Empire of Giganos.
35:
UCE Vice Foreign
Minister. Heedless of
danger, she keeps up
peace talks to settle
conflicts everywhere.
She is also of the royal
line of the Sanc
Kingdom, which
preached total pacifism.
36:
Queen of the Kingdom of
Na, exiled from the other
world of Byston Well.

She also commands the
battleship Gran-Garan.
Since her exile, she aids
the UCE to defend the
surface from the Drake
Army, which has set out
to conquer it.
37:
Commander of the
Poseidal Army's Imperial
Guard. Brainwashed and
controlled through
Poseidal's Bio-Relation.
Sent to the Earth Sphere
to watch Giwaza, leader
of the expedition.
38:
Eiji's older sister.
Urging harmony between
Grados and Earth people,
she gives spiritual
support to Earthlings in
Grados-ruled North
America.
39:
A popular idol singer on
the battleship Macross.
She debuted aboard the
Macross on its way back
to Earth.
Her voice soothes the
people longing to return
to Earth.
40:
Domon Kasshu's older
brother.
He stole the Devil
Gundam mid-research
and fled.
Nothing has been heard
of them since.
41:
A former Zeon ace pilot
once feared as the
"Nightmare of Solomon."

He still fights the UCE
as a member of the Zeon
Remnants.

He has also been
confirmed as the one
who stole Gundam Unit 2
from the UCE.
42:
Humanoid mobile
weapons that became the
mainstay of close combat
once Minovsky particles
made visual-range
fighting the norm.
Anaheim Electronics now
handles all their
development. Reliable,
they are fielded in great
numbers by friend and
foe alike, such as the
Federation and former
Principality of Zeon.
43:
Humanoid mobile
weapons built by
Giganos. Via Dr. Lang
Plato, who defected to
Earth, Dragonar-1 and
the other D-series units
fell into UCE hands.
They can mount and
detach an atmospheric
flight unit (Lifter).
44:
Machines born by
revival (rebirth) from the
Organic Plates that
Orphan produces.
Humans can board and
operate them.
Organic Machines fall
into two broad types:
Grand Chers and Brain
Powerds.
45:
Humanoid mobile
weapons developed by
Nergal Heavy Industries.
They can switch to
combat frames suited to
each situation, such as
ground, air or space
combat. Fitted with the
IFS (Image Feedback
System), they put far
less control strain on the
pilot than earlier
humanoid weapons.
They run on gravity
wave energy sent from
their mothership.
46:
Humanoid mobile
weapons, the Dunbine
among them, made in the
other world of Byston
Well. Their armor and
drive systems use the
shells and muscle of
great beasts native there.
They run on an energy
called Aura Power.
47:
Humanoid mobile
weapons made in the
Pentagona World. They
feature movable frames
with separate armor and
drive mechanisms, and
beam coating against
optical weapons.
Ranked A-class to B-class
by performance, the
L-Gaim is an A-class
Heavy Metal.
48:
Humanoid mobile
weapons with a
three-stage variable
mechanism.
They can take the
jet-type Fighter,
humanoid Battroid or
in-between GERWALK
mode, and their greatest
strength is adapting
flexibly to any battle.
They were completed
using the Macross's
overtechnology, then
rolled out as the
battleship Macross's
carrier craft.
49:
General-purpose
humanoid mobile
weapons made by
Grados. A backpack
attachment system lets
them swap in various
weapons. The backpack
also holds a system that
instantly adapts the unit
to its environment, such
as ground or space.
50:
Gundam-type humanoid
mobile weapons made
just for the Gundam
Fight.
Built for martial-arts
melee, their chief feature
is the Mobile Trace
System, which links the
pilot's moves directly to
the machine.
So a pilot's fighting skill
counts far more than
piloting skill.
51:
The collective name for
the special machines
appearing in many
places since conflict
flared up again.
Each has an unmanned
control program and
high combat ability.
All of them have been
confirmed to be leaked
machines once developed
by the UCE.
52:
Humanoid mobile
weapons developed by
the UCE itself.
They were begun with
the goal of a UCE force
of its own, free of its
members' troops and
entanglements. Applying
basic research from past
projects, they were built
as cheap, reliable units.
53:
Another world that lies
between the sea and the
land.
It is said to be a haven
where souls whose lives
on the surface world
have ended rest until
they are reborn there.
Byston Well is sustained
by the Aura Power that
living things give off.
Humanoid mobile
weapons driven by this
power are called Aura
Machines.
The Gran-Garan and the
Drake Army came to the
surface from this world.
54:
A world of five planets
in outer space.
It is now ruled by a
person named Oldna
Poseidal.
It is also the homeland
of Daba Myroad and his
companions.
55:
A type of railgun, a
device that accelerates
and launches massive
objects such as
meteorites.

It is meant for shipping
resources mined on the
Moon to Earth.
Giganos, however, has
turned it into a weapon
for dropping massive
meteorites onto Earth.
56:
Super-ancient ruins
found in a Pacific Ocean
trench.
In truth, it is a living
spaceship that came to
Earth from space
hundreds of thousands
of years ago.
Its whole hull is also an
Organic Engine that
artificially makes
Organic Energy, the
energy of living things,
and it runs on the
energy it makes.
The Reclaimers are
readying it to fly off to
the galaxy, but it is said
that as it leaves Earth it
will drain the world's
Organic Energy, and
every living thing will
die.
57:
A kind of instant
teleportation based on
overtechnology, used by
the Jovian Lizards to
attack Earth. Living
things such as humans
are known to be unable
to withstand it. It has
also been found that a
Boson Jump is space-time
travel into the past via
the ruin unit on Mars,
followed by a return to
the present.
58:
A show within "Martian
Successor Nadesico."
A 39-episode anime made
on Earth long ago.
It shows Gekiganger's
hot-blooded fight for
justice against an evil
group bent on world
conquest.
Popular in the Jovian
Federation, which has
little entertainment, it is
now called the Jovians'
scripture.
59:
A wartime treaty signed
by the UCE and the
Principality of Zeon in
the One Year War.
Its main terms ban NBC
and genocidal weapons
and combat in neutral
zones, and set rules for
treating prisoners.
It is named for being
signed in Antarctica.
60:
The first intelligent life
in cosmic history,
creator of the Zentradi
(Meltrandi), giant
humanoid bioweapons
for war.
It built into its soldiers
the basic directive
"Never lay a hand on the
Protoculture," but in
time lost control and was
wiped out by the two
races it made.
Humanity was also made
as a Protoculture
subspecies, so humans,
Zentradi and Meltrandi
share a common
ancestor.
61:
A plate much like the
plates found in Orphan.
Its surface bears
carvings that look like
writing.
62:
The evolved form of the
Ultimate Cells that make
up the Devil Gundam.

Living metal cells that
multiply by fusing with
organic cells.
Humans infected with
these cells fall under the
Devil Gundam's control.
63:
A UCE strategic support
system built on the
concept "a unit with
maximum firepower that
keeps a single weapon's
mobility and versatility."

A high-mobility unit fit
even for close combat
controls several combat
satellites around Earth
for heavy bombardment.
The satellites have
abilities today's
technology cannot copy,
and no development
records remain.
64:
An Earth Federation
Government project to
build defenses against
forces from outer space.
Research began under
Dr. Albert Rainen as
head of development.
Units using old-war-era
defense satellites were
developed, but an
accident just before
deployment effectively
ended it.
Dr. Rainen went missing.
The accident was blamed
on a design error, but in
truth Federation radicals
staged it to purge the
old faction.
65:
An energy substance
inside the internal
engine of the satellite
Guardian. It holds vast
energy and can recharge
itself autonomously.
The Guardian can run
semi-permanently
because a perpetual
engine using this
substance is at work.
It has been studied in
various past projects,
but its nature remains
unclear.
66:
The Giganos military's
ultimate weapon, built
on the Moon's far side.
A mind-control system
called biofeedback gives
it Metal Armor-class
mobility. Its skull-like
form, bristling with
beam cannons, missiles
and more, overwhelms all
foes.
67:
A name based on pair
production in quantum
mechanics: the idea that
Orphan, too, must have a
counterpart somewhere.

Yet no such "B-Plate" has
ever been confirmed.

Thought to be the key to
Orphan's rising, it fuels
an escalating fight over
plates between the
Reclaimers and the Novis
Noah, each seeking it
first.
68:
One of the UCE's bases
in space.
Once called Solomon, it
was renamed after the
old war.
To show its prestige to
the Zeon remnants and
the public, the
Federation faction
gathers the UCE's main
warships there for a
large naval review.
It is also a place of
bitter history, taken by
the Federation of old at
the end of its fight with
the former Zeon.
